comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"520cd1febab68ed266da0eee8b03bef97a52ac0227ba1d5e77ba448c28f348e9"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Fallback — The page refused to load in the run browser:⁠ main document returned HTTP 403

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Reported defect is a behavioral annoyance on jkanime.net (a click opens an unrelated site in a new tab), but every browser attempt to reach the site returned an HTTP 403 "Just a moment..." interstitial, so the click could not be rehearsed and no candidate could be validated; the best candidate is carried for human review.

## Candidate for review

`jkanime.net#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')`

BaseFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt

Not verified: Browser access to the reported page was exhausted before any evidence could be collected:⁠ all three navigation attempts (control session without extension on desktop, prepared AdGuard extension v5.5.2.3 with filters 2/3/19 on desktop, and the same prepared session on a materially different mobile profile) returned HTTP 403 with the title 'Just a moment...' and an interstitial URL, and the third returned technical_attempt_budget_exhausted. No DOM, network inventory or click rehearsal was obtainable, so the reported click-to-popup symptom could neither be reproduced nor shown absent, apply_rule never ran and no visual review or page-integrity verdict exists for this candidate. Note also that jkanime.net is already listed in the shared BaseFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt rule for scriptlet("abort-on-property-read", "popjs"), which a maintainer should check first.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44964840031

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `5a5cbd6`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"69bba2e30df4dddc4bd3a5488f6f479172eb33b42f28ae59dfa2358ac2f0f593"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The left-rail SkinRave banners reported on steamcommunity.com/market are not served by the page:⁠ it loaded fine in both an unfiltered Chromium session and the reporter's exact filter configuration, with all 883 requests going to Steam/Fastly hosts, no "Remove ads" text, and the site's own centred 940px market layout containing no ad rail. The reporter's screenshot also shows Steam Inventory Helper's own "SIH Features"/"SIH Games" items injected into Steam's header, so the banners most likely come from an extension in the reporter's browser rather than from the site (hypothesis, not proven).

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's closing rules do not cover this report:⁠ it is a plain ads report, not a first-party-ad case, a paywall, a German anti-adblock wall, another anti-adblock wall, or a scam/phishing page, so no policy rule blocks rule generation. Rule generation is allowed; the closure rests on the observed absence of the reported defect, not on a policy block.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44969521690

The reported defect was not reproduced

Indeterminate — The "Advertisement" card over the PetrolSpy map does not render in a session using the reporter's own AdGuard filters:⁠ the site's AdSense loader (pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js) is already blocked by the existing AdGuard Base rule ||pagead2.googlesyndication.com^, leaving no ad and no blank slot. No new rule is needed, so the issue is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

No policy rule of the run instruction blocks rule generation here:⁠ the report is an ordinary ad report from a mobile app's network-level filtering, not a first-party-ad, paywall, anti-adblock, or scam case. No rule is generated because the ad-serving request behind the reported overlay is already stopped by an existing AdGuard Base filter rule, so the reported defect did not reproduce on the loaded page.

comment.body:
Report from SWIM's signed-in session, since the automated run couldn't reach playback.

On the close recommendation: these breaks are mostly paid third-party commercials stitched into the stream (video ads under the filter policy), not self-promotion, and the existing `||mt.ssai.peacocktv.com^` entry suggests Peacock's SSAI is already treated that way. That entry just doesn't match the current flow, because ad breaks now load from different paths. These rules blocked the ads in testing (Chrome 154, Browser Extension 5.5.4.76 MV3; also Chrome 128):

```
/mm/master.psf$xmlhttprequest,domain=peacocktv.com
/intadsvod/ads.json$xmlhttprequest,domain=peacocktv.com
/atp/*/cmaf_$xmlhttprequest,domain=peacocktv.com
```

The player retries once, then resumes content. The pre-roll slot shows a brief black screen. The rules don't touch content media, content manifests or DRM requests. Modifying the `.psf` response instead stalled playback.

One possible side effect: switching episodes inside the player sometimes leaves the previous episode's audio playing and starts the next one mid-timeline. A page reload avoids it. Cause unconfirmed!

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On apkapp.ru the reporter's boxed blank band (and two identical ones in the article and above the comments) are Yandex RTB ad wrappers that keep a reserved 200px height after the existing generic rule `##div[id^="yandex_rtb"]` hides the ad inside them. Adding `apkapp.ru##div[style^="min-height"]:has(> div[id^="yandex_rtb"])` collapses all three, and the reporter-profile experiment verified the symptom resolved with page integrity intact. ## Rule `apkapp.ru##div[style^="min-height"]:has(> div[id^="yandex_rtb"])` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is not the site's own first-party advertising:⁠ the blank bands are the residual footprint of third-party Yandex RTB ad units whose creatives an existing generic rule already hides. It is not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock case at all — the page renders normally with no detector or overlay (browser evidence:⁠ no anti-adblock signal, page obstruction none). Not a scam/phishing/malware report; it is an ordinary leftover-layout annoyance open to rule generation. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5a5cbd637c00de45b6b7792ebc4363177bf03326/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The circled target is a native in-feed app-install ad (Audible) inside the ASKEN Android app's own diary screen, not on the recorded play.google.com listing, which loaded clean (HTTP 200, no ad surface, 0 ad slots). The ad-serving request comes from the app itself and is invisible to the locked browser/proxy environment, so no host can be evidenced and any rule would be guesswork; a maintainer needs an app-side traffic capture to write a Mobile filter network rule.

## Missing information

- No way to capture in-app (non-browser) traffic for AdGuard-for-Android in-app ad reports: Issue #⁠247791 reports a native in-feed ad rendered inside the Android app jp.co.greenhouse.asken (reporter screenshot shows the app's own diary screen), while the recorded issue URL is only the app's Google Play listing. The locked adguard_cli environment exposes a filtering proxy for browser navigation plus apply_rule phases; it offers no path to observe the HTTPS requests an Android app emits for its in-app ad SDK, and the reported Play Store page contains no such ad surface (HTTP 200, no 'Audible'/'インストール' text, 0 iframes, 0 ad slots). Without the ad-serving host from an app-side capture, no network or cosmetic rule can be evidenced. What is missing is either (a) an app-traffic capture channel (AdGuard for Android filtering log / HAR from the reporter's device) in the run tooling, or (b) instruction guidance on how in-app ad reports whose URL is a store listing should be classified when the ad surface is unreachable from the browser.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On studyhacker.net articles the AdGuard Social filter hides the Facebook/X/Hatena/Threads/LINE share buttons but leaves their wrapper, so only the 「リンクをコピー」(⧉) button remains visible — the leftover the reporter's arrow marks, repeated in the top share row and in the 「この記事をシェア」 section at the article end. One cosmetic rule hiding both share-widget containers verified in the reporter's filter set (symptom resolved, page intact, no remaining instances). ## Rule `studyhacker.net##.share-preview-top, section.share-preview-bottom` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and undocumented anti-adblock walls; none applies here — this is a social share widget whose buttons the AdGuard Social filter already blocks, with the wrapper and its copy-link button left visible. Filter policy's Social media filter purpose explicitly covers share buttons on third-party sites, so blocking the widget wrapper that would otherwise show a lone copy-link control is an allowed social-widget rule. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5a5cbd637c00de45b6b7792ebc4363177bf03326/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 6095](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5a5cbd637c00de45b6b7792ebc4363177bf03326/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L6095). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on sberbs.ru is a fixed cookie-consent bar (`div.cookie.test`) that the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter does not cover; adding sberbs.ru to the existing shared `.cookie` element-hiding rule in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt hides it, verified in the CLI-proxy before/after phases with the page left intact. ## Rule `sberbs.ru##.cookie` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party ads, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls; this report is a cookie-consent notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle (policy:⁠ 'Cookie Notices — Purpose:⁠ this filter blocks cookie notices on web pages'). Not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page shows no detector and no anti-adblock script appears in the network inventory. Maintainer rule applied:⁠ the `.cookie` selector already exists in a shared multi-domain element-hiding rule, so the reported domain is added to that rule instead of a new per-site rule; the candidate is submitted scoped to sberbs.ru for the host to merge. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5a5cbd637c00de45b6b7792ebc4363177bf03326/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 3612](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5a5cbd637c00de45b6b7792ebc4363177bf03326/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L3612). ## Screenshots

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported sticky Bloomberg "Cyber Sale" subscription footer banner did not render on bloomberg.com in either an unfiltered control Chromium session or the AdGuard-extension baseline session (reporter's filter set):⁠ no matching element or text exists in the DOM at load or after scrolling to the page bottom, and structured full-page vision reported the symptom absent with an unobstructed page. No rule can be written for an element the site never served, so the report is recommended for closing as not reproduced.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script; none of them applies to this subscription-promo annoyance report, so rule generation is permitted. The repository's own policy document lets the Other Annoyances filter block website self-promotion 'if it is considered an annoying element', decided rule-by-rule by developers, and the repository already keeps bloomberg.com subscription rules in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt (for example bloomberg.com#⁠#⁠#⁠plug-banner-outlet). No rule is proposed because the reported banner was not served in either the unfiltered control session or the filtered baseline session, so no selector could be validated.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44987798689

comment.body:
@AdamWr Thanks for looking into this and for the changes in `23ee3a2`. Could you reopen this issue? I can still reproduce the problem on two separate iPhones running iOS 27.2.1 and AdGuard for iOS 4.5.25.

**What I see in Safari**

When I open `https://www.theverge.com/`, a full-screen pop-up says **“Please allow ads on this site.”** It covers the homepage and prevents me from accessing the site. The pop-up is the one associated with `report.error-report.com` in the automated analysis above. The original report includes a screenshot and my filter configuration.

**What I tested on iPhone**

- **Filter updates.** The warning still appeared after I updated my AdGuard filters at about **9 p.m. Eastern on November 21**. It also persisted after the **10:09 p.m. Eastern** iOS Base filter build was published. The public optimized iOS Base filter **2.5.6.24** contains all three changes from `23ee3a2`. I don’t have the exact installed build recorded for every test.
- **AdGuard-only test.** After the approximately 9 p.m. update, I opened the homepage in a fresh Safari private tab with **uBlock Origin Lite and AdGuard DNS Protection both disabled**. AdGuard Safari Protection and Advanced Protection were enabled in the app, and the same full-screen warning appeared. I didn’t separately verify the AdGuard web extension’s Private Browsing permission for that test.
- **Second iPhone and website data.** I reproduced the warning on a second iPhone with the same iOS and AdGuard versions. I deleted Safari website data for The Verge on **both** phones and tested again. The same warning still blocked access on both.
- **Allowlist and protections off.** Adding The Verge to AdGuard’s Safari allowlist did not clear the warning. In earlier troubleshooting, the homepage loaded after I turned off AdGuard Safari Protection, AdGuard DNS Protection, and uBlock Origin Lite together.
- **Suggested iframe rule.** I tried `theverge.com##iframe[src^="https://report.error-report.com/modal"]` in AdGuard’s Safari User rules. The full-screen pop-up was replaced by a native Safari alert saying **“Please allow ads on this site. Click OK to learn more.”** Tapping **Cancel** brought the same alert back repeatedly. Tapping **OK** returned me to the original full-screen warning. The homepage remained inaccessible.

**What I see on other devices**

- **Mac, Firefox:** I saw the same access-blocking pop-up in recent days. The homepage now loads without the pop-up with the regular **uBlock Origin** extension still enabled. DNS Protection and Stealth Mode are off. I don’t know what changed on the Mac.
- **Vision Pro:** The homepage loads with free AdGuard and uBlock enabled.

Could you verify whether all three rules from `23ee3a2` reach AdGuard for iOS 4.5.25, whether Advanced Protection applies them before The Verge’s detector runs, and whether they match the script served to iPhone Safari? If there’s a specific diagnostic log or setting that would help confirm which rules ran, please let me know.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Wikipedia's multilingual portal (www⁠.wikipedia.org) still shows a large Wikimedia fundraising overlay panel ("Donate now" / "I already donated", "The internet is changing.", $2.75 ask) over the page even with all reported AdGuard lists enabled, because no published rule targets its wrapper class. The single domain-scoped element-hiding rule `wikipedia.org##.overlay-banner` hides the whole overlay and was verified by the bound experiment (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no residue, no remaining instances). ## Rule `wikipedia.org##.overlay-banner` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a donation/self-promotion overlay on the site's own page, not the site's third-party advertising:⁠ the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter's stated purpose is to "block self-promotion of websites" when considered annoying, and the repository already keeps Wikipedia's donation rules there (`wikipedia.org##.donate-banner`, `wikipedia.org#$#.cn-fundraising`, `wikipedia.org#$#.frb-overlay-open`). None of the instruction's closing rules applies:⁠ this is not the site's own third-party advertising, not a paywall (the portal content is fully visible and free behind the overlay), not a German anti-adblock wall and not an anti-adblock wall at all (the page showed no detector, no ad-blocker message, and get_network_log contains no third-party detector script). The banner is a same-domain, in-page annoyance request set with no third-party vendor host to extend, so a domain-scoped cosmetic rule is the repository-shaped fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d44e8a308c35cda172fc128be50134f2c33bd370/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

It is served in the site's own HTML with no third-party CMP host, so a domain-scoped element-hiding rule removes it:⁠ `xmartserver.com##.cookies-card`. The candidate passed the A/B/C proxy experiment (`environmentExperiment: verified`) and the vision review (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no remaining instances, no damage), with complete full-page vision from the CLI-proxied session. ## Rule `xmartserver.com##.cookies-card` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's policy closes first-party advertising, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls; this report is none of those — it is a cookie-consent notice, the annoyance category the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for. It is not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page shows only the consent card, no detector script was captured and no anti-adblock rule acted (get_applied_rules). <!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"5e50bdaaf3ddd71fdb0767731b96dbabc3355b2540bab0af36b63d8639f04a96"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported blank advertising band labelled "Реклама" on iz.ru did not reproduce:⁠ with the repository's filters applied the page shows no blank ad band or placeholder (structured full-page vision reports the symptom absent with zero instances), all twelve AdFox "Реклама" slots collapse to zero area through existing iz.ru rules, and no ad-exchange request is made, even after a reload. Recommend closing as not reproduced, noting the check ran through the AdGuard CLI proxy in Chromium rather than the reporter's Safari and that a narrower-viewport attempt was refused with HTTP 403.

## Policy rationale

No rule of the repository policy stated in the run instruction blocks this report:⁠ it is not the site's own first-party advertising offer, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock detector without a captured detector script; rule generation would have been allowed had the defect reproduced. The close carries reproduction status not_reproduced, not a policy block.

## Missing information

- Reporter settings import cannot be applied in the adguard_cli environment: The issue carries a reporter settings import URL (reports.adguard.app/settings/import.html?product_type=mac...), which the run instruction says makes the reporter profile `reported_on_current`. In the locked adguard_cli environment, browser sessions must be launched with extension:⁠"none", and launch_browser rejects any `settings` payload for such a session ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠""). The CLI proxy only exposes the repository's official filter baseline (AdGuard Russian/Base/Tracking/Social/Experimental/Mobile Ads/DNS/URL Tracking/Cookie/Popups/Mobile App Banners/Other Annoyances/Widgets/Mail Tracking) and explicitly skips the third-party catalogs the reporter also had (EasyList, EasyPrivacy, Fanboy's Annoyances, RU AdList:⁠ Counters, etc.), plus the reporter's two userscripts (AdGuard Extra, Popup Blocker) and Stealth settings. So the reporter's exact configuration could not be reproduced; every observation in this run comes from the official-filter CLI baseline in an extension-less Chromium session, not from AdGuard for Mac v2.20.3 in Safari.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45003221011

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — keeb-finder.com renders a first-party "Cookies &⁠ analytics" consent card fixed at the bottom-right that covers the Black Friday Deals product cards on load; the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, enabled in the reporter's config, has no rule for this site. Hiding the card with keeb-finder.com#⁠#⁠[⁠aria-labelledby="cookie-banner-title"]⁠ was verified by the bound A/B/C experiment (element visible before, hidden after, page integrity intact, no residue). ## Rule `keeb-finder.com##[aria-labelledby="cookie-banner-title"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules do not apply:⁠ this is not the site's own advertising (no ad creative involved), not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall of any kind — the page's overlay is a cookie/analytics consent card. The defect is an annoyance overlay served from the site's own HTML, the exact category the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for, so rule generation is allowed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/da0f85bd781a01728b798214dd15c2336546d0e1/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45010015617 Automated analysis against filters at `da0f85b`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
iOS is known to sometimes inject certain rules too late, but I tested it and couldn't reproduce the issue with up-to-date filters.

I also checked it on Windows using both the AdGuard app and browser extension, and I couldn't reproduce the issue there either.

Which filter list or settings trigger the detection?
Please also check whether the issue persists with DNS filtering, third-party filter lists (those that don't have "AdGuard" in their name), and other ad blockers disabled.

comment.body:
### Issue URL (Ads) [https://www.sheepesports.com/en/all](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sheepesports.com%2Fen%2Fall) ### Comment > ## Summary > Follow-up to #247536 (fixed on Nov 19). The sponsor logo in the header of `sheepesports.com` is still not blocked, on any platform. > > ## Sponsor logo in the header > - **Where:** right of the menu button on mobile; after the divider in the navbar on desktop > - **What:** an advertiser's logo linking to the advertiser. The site picks it in its own JS based on the visitor's country: > > | When | Sponsor | Link | > |---|---|---| > | Most countries (seen from Turkey) | Polymarket | `https://polymarket.com` | > | Rocket League pages (`/en/rl`, RL articles) | Michelin | `https://www.michelin.com/en/media/magazine/michelin-video-game-rocket-league` | > | France (from the site's JS, not seen live) | Winamax | `winamax.fr/registration/landing/sheep_esports?banid=...` | > > The logo is the site's own image, so DNS/network rules can't block it. > > ## Steps to reproduce > 1. Open https://www.sheepesports.com/en/all > 2. Right of the menu button → Polymarket logo > 3. Open https://www.sheepesports.com/en/rl → Michelin logo in the same spot > > ## Suggested rules > The Polymarket rule was tested on iPhone (Safari + AdGuard for iOS). > > ```adblock > sheepesports.com##a[href="https://polymarket.com"] > sheepesports.com##a[href*="michelin-video-game-rocket-league"] > sheepesports.com##a[href*="winamax.fr/registration/landing/sheep_esports"] > sheepesports.com##.border-l:has(> a[href="https://polymarket.com"], > a[href*="michelin-video-game-rocket-league"], > a[href*="winamax.fr/registration/landing/sheep_esports"]) > ``` > > ## Minor: leftover gap after the #247536 fix > `sheepesports.com##.bg-brand-surface[style^="aspect-ratio"]` hides the ad box but leaves its wrapper, which adds an extra ~16px gap where each ad was on the homepage and game hubs (see screenshots: double gap under the top story). This rule hides the wrapper too. It only matches wrappers that contain nothing but ad boxes: > > ```adblock > sheepesports.com##.justify-center:has(> .rounded-card.bg-brand-surface[style^="aspect-ratio"]) > ``` > > Tested in a 390×844 viewport on the homepage, `/en/rl` and 3 articles; nothing else matched. > > Screenshots attached. > > GitHub: `@vurijj` ``` Username: @vurijj ``` ### Screenshots
Screenshot 1 ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/enxqkrj3ovswwo8ooc0og8wwwk44wg0pf2ko59h6m8.png?nc=1)
Screenshot 2 ![Screenshot 2](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/ccae0yuvijkg4c0gssksc048s84444ol611w4sa3o0.png?nc=1)

issue.title: 39macvartv.live
issue.body:
### Issue URL (Ads) [https://39macvartv.live/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2F39macvartv.live%2F) ### Comment > ## Summary > `39macvartv.live` has a rotating domain. The site's own header says the next domain will be the same name with the number +1 (40macvartv.live, ...). With the AdGuard Turkish filter on, the "Mr. Bahis" betting ads are still visible. > > ## What's left > | Where | What | Element | > |---|---|---| > | Top bar | Mr. Bahis social links (`heylink.me/mrbahissosyal`) | `.header-top` | > | Header | Mr. Bahis logo (`logo.png`) | `header .logo` | > | Footer | Mr. Bahis logo again | `footer img[src$="logo.png"]` | > | Player poster | "Yayın başlıyor" image (`yayinbasliyor.png`) with the Mr. Bahis logo baked into the top-left corner | `.player-poster` background | > | During playback | Mr. Bahis watermark linking to `heylink.me/mrbahisguncel` (inside the `channel?id=...` iframe) | `#watermark` | > | Before the stream | Video pre-roll ad with a 5s skip button | network | > > The player config (`channel?id=zirve`, Zirve Stream template): > ``` > prerollVideo:'http://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lookatusdoweneedu/v/zirve/mrbahispreroll.mp4' > watermarkImage:'logo.png', watermarkLink:'https://heylink.me/mrbahisguncel/' > posterImage:'yayinbasliyor.png' > ``` > If the pre-roll fails to load, the player's `PLAYER_ERROR` handler skips straight to the stream, so blocking it doesn't break playback. > > ## Steps to reproduce > 1. Open https://39macvartv.live/ (or the current number) > 2. Logo in the header and footer, icons in the top bar, logo on the player poster > 3. Press play → pre-roll ad, then the watermark on the stream > > Note: on desktop the pre-roll only plays once per browser session (sessionStorage key `preroll_watched`), so use a private window to see it again. > > ## Suggested rules > Same domain regex as the existing `[$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##.footer-links`. Tested with the AdGuard Browser Extension in Firefox on 39macvartv.live: only the listed elements are hidden; the player, match list and footer text stay. The pre-roll rule is based on the player config. > > ```adblock > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##.header-top > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##header .logo > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##footer img[src$="logo.png"] > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]###watermark > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]#$#.player-poster { background-image: none !important; } > ||cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lookatusdoweneedu/v/*preroll*.mp4 > ``` > > Screenshots attached. > > GitHub: `@vurijj` ``` Username: @vurijj ``` ### Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Turkish filter already hides this site's banner creatives, but the Mr. Bahis logos and social links survive; a browser-verified domain-scoped hide of `.social-area` plus `img[src$="logo.png"]` cleared the header logo, footer logo, top-bar social row and watermark with no damage, yet the report stays open because the same logo is baked into the player's "Yayın başlıyor" poster, which only a separate CSS-injection rule for the player frame can strip and which cannot be verified against the reported URL.

## Still visible after the rule

- Player poster — top-left of the 'YAYIN BAŞLIYOR!' panel — The MR Bahis winged logo and 'MR BAHIS' wordmark are visible baked into the top-left corner of the 'YAYIN BAŞLIYOR!' player poster. The branded player placeholder panel remains visible in the content column.
- Main content column, “YAYIN BAŞLIYOR!” player poster, top-left corner — The Mr. Bahis winged logo is visibly baked into the top-left corner of the “YAYIN BAŞLIYOR!” player poster/placeholder image, so the operator branding identified in the poster part of the symptom remains visible.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

comment.body: I can reproduce this. The bot didn't see the ads because they're gated behind a cookie. **Why it wasn't reproduced:** the `filmplus` theme loads all ads from its own first-party endpoint, `/wp-content/themes/filmplus/ads-data.php`, but `blocks.js` only renders them once the cookie `stf_v=1` exists. That cookie is set by a 300-second countdown (`gecit.sure: 300`) that starts when the player goes fullscreen on desktop, or when the player is tapped on mobile. After that, the ads stay for 365 days (`gecit.gun: 365`). A fresh session never sees them. **To reproduce:** on https://www.fullhdfilmizle.fit/ run `document.cookie = 'stf_v=1;path=/'` in the console and reload (screenshot attached, AdGuard Browser Extension in Firefox with AdGuard Base and AdGuard Turkish enabled). Then the endpoint's slots render: - `deri`: Herkulbet page skin (`stads.cfd/ads/herkulbet-1920x1200-v4-min.webp`) plus a full-screen click overlay `a.stf-bg-hit` → `t2m.co/fulllhdfilm` (1100px+ wide) - `hdr`: SoloBet banner under the menu (`stads.cfd/ads/solobet-*.webp` → `soloaff.site`) - `pu` / `pa`: Kralbet banners above and below the player on movie pages (`stads.cfd/ads/kralbet-*.webp` → `t.ly/eIdFo`) - `popup`: a click anywhere outside links and buttons opens `t.ly/eIdFo` in a 1×1 popup window, once every 6 hours (tab-under on mobile) None of the existing `fullhdfilmizle.*` rules in the Turkish filter catch this ad system. **Suggested rules:** ```adblock /wp-content/themes/filmplus/ads-data.php$domain=fullhdfilmizle.* ||stads.cfd^ ``` Tested in Firefox with the AdGuard Browser Extension and `stf_v=1` set: with these rules nothing renders and the player still works. Blocking `ads-data.php` alone should be enough, since everything above is built from its response; a simulated failed request left no slots, skin, click overlay or popup handler. `vq.js` catches the failed request and falls back to no video ads, and `blocks.js` only logs a warning. `stads.cfd` hosts the ad images and is a backup in case the data ever comes through another way.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The report's annoyance is the Google follow prompt ("ABEMA TIMES をGoogleでフォロー", loaded with news.google.com/swg) that the reporter's arrow points at on the ABEMA TIMES article:⁠ a full-width row between the article date line and the article text, repeated in the footer. It is not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ no detector script, no overlay gate, and the page was fully readable and scrollable in every phase. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The IKEA Poland homepage keeps showing its cookie-consent panel because the repository blocks IKEA's first-party consent-UI script only for the English locale path. Extending that block to the Polish path (||ikea.com/*/cookieconsent/v2/scripts/consent-ui.$domain=ikea.com) was verified in the reporter-profile session:⁠ the panel is gone and the page is intact. ## Rule `||ikea.com/*/cookieconsent/v2/scripts/consent-ui.$domain=ikea.com` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance:⁠ not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German or other anti-adblock wall. The page shows no adblock detection:⁠ get_applied_rules lists no anti-adblock rule, the HAR has zero blocked requests, and no overlay asks the user to disable the blocker. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7daf805c9b5d41a777d05abe37181b78da4b6b47/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report is a click-driven ad popunder:⁠ the reported page embeds a third-party player frame from ondemand.to, and every click on that player makes the frame log a Monetag click event (ondemand.to/pf.gif?...e=click...n=monetag) followed by a "nopop" event, while an ad click-through tab opened in the reporter's Chrome. The click never opened a tab in this run's browser (0 pages opened in all apply_rule phases), so the scriptlet fix ondemand.to#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('prevent-window-open') could not be verified and is left for human review.

Adding smotrim.ru#⁠#⁠.adfox-topline was verified:⁠ the band is gone, the header moves to the top, and headings, media and controls are unchanged. ## Rule `smotrim.ru##.adfox-topline` ## Policy rationale The leftover container belongs to a third-party ad network (Yandex adfox), not to the site's own advertising; the ad SDK requests yandex.ru/ads/system/context.js and header-bidding.js are blocked by a general Base filter rule and the empty container is residue of that blocking. The report involves no paywall and no anti-adblock wall, so no policy exception closes it. The rule is an element-hiding rule on a stable ad-specific class, domain-scoped, verified with no page-integrity regression. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7daf805c9b5d41a777d05abe37181b78da4b6b47/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 162](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7daf805c9b5d41a777d05abe37181b78da4b6b47/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt#L162). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The "Singles aus Rosenheim" sidebar box is an empty ad leftover:⁠ its icony dating widget loads js.icony.com/api.js in the unfiltered control, but that loader is blocked by the German filter, leaving the heading over a blank block. Hiding #⁠id-Container-458253 removes it with page integrity intact, yet the bound vision review kept refusing because other ad-blocking whitespace in the same column (the site's 1px separator rules around ad slots already hidden by the Base filter, and the empty "Live:⁠ Top-Artikel" module) remains, which only a site-wide separator rewrite would clear.

## Candidate for review

`rosenheim24.de###id-Container-458253`

GermanFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: Both apply_rule experiments ended environmentExperiment=inconclusive with visualReview verdict 'rejected', adLayoutResidue 'present', pageIntegrity 'intact' and observedDamage empty. The review confirmed the candidate removes the module it names (phase B:⁠ selector visible, phase C:⁠ hidden; domChecks measured display:⁠none / 0px height) but refused it for leftover whitespace elsewhere in the same sidebar column:⁠ the site's own 1px hr.id-Container-separator rules around ad wrappers whose placeholders are already hidden by the Base rule #⁠#⁠div[⁠data-id-advertdfpconf]⁠, and the heading-only 'Live:⁠ Top-Artikel unserer Leser' module (#⁠id-Container-459107). Clearing that band needs hiding the site's own separators or the sidebar tail, a site-wide design change out of scope for this report; the reported module removal itself is mechanically proven.

## Still visible after the rule

- Right sidebar below the '⁠> Alle Partyfotos <⁠' module (Live:⁠ Top-Artikel unserer Leser area) — Large empty white reserved sidebar block with several thin horizontal separator rules and no heading or article content visible; residual leftover space from the blocked/empty sidebar module.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3
